# id

Print the current process credentials on Linux.

## Usage

```sh
moonx cli/id -G
```

## Common options

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED OPTIONS -->
<!-- Generated by tools/metadata from options.json. -->

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `-u`, `--user` | Print only the user ID. |
| `-g`, `--group` | Print only the group ID. |
| `-G`, `--groups` | Print all group IDs. |
| `-r`, `--real` | Select the real user or group ID. |
| `-n`, `--name` | Print names from the local account database. |
| `-z`, `--zero` | Terminate entries with NUL. |
| `--help` | Show help. |
| `--version` | Show the version. |
<!-- END GENERATED OPTIONS -->

## Notes

Reads real and effective IDs and supplementary groups from /proc/self/status. Names require an authoritative local files database. The default security-context report and named-user queries are unsupported.

See the [compatibility guide](../../docs/compatibility.md) for the supported profile.
